title: On keeping records
excerpt: A group that has traded since 1989 accumulates more history than it writes down. A note on why this Chronicle exists.
body: Most of what a company does is never recorded anywhere. A decision gets taken in a corridor, works, and becomes simply how things are done — until nobody remembers that it was ever a decision at all.

That is usually harmless and occasionally expensive. Practices survive their reasons. A standard held for good cause in one decade becomes a habit defended on grounds nobody can quite articulate in the next.

This Chronicle is an attempt at the modest version of a remedy: writing down how the group approaches its work while the reasoning is still available, rather than reconstructing it later from results.

It is not a history and it is not a record of achievements. It is closer to a set of working notes, kept in the open, on the assumption that reasoning stated plainly is easier to challenge — and easier to correct — than reasoning left implicit.
